title: Speculative decoding + model integration: draft acceptance & rollback plan
content:
Purpose and scope

This draft outlines the design and operational plan for introducing speculative decoding into the serving runtime and the model integration workflow that accompanies it. It focuses on how speculative decoding interacts with kernels, scheduler policies, and the KV cache, and defines acceptance criteria, rollback procedures, and telemetry required to safely ship at scale.

Background and motivation

Speculative decoding provides a low-latency optimization by generating candidate tokens using a smaller, faster model or cheaper decoding path while the full model computes the final token. The approach reduces tail latency for many workloads, but introduces new failure modes: quality regressions, cache mismatches, and resource contention with regular inferences. We need a controlled integration path that limits blast radius, provides observable metrics for quality and cost, and supports safe rollback.

Design overview

1) Components involved
- Serving runtime kernel selection: the runtime may choose execution kernels that favor throughput or latency. Speculative paths must be mapped to low latency kernels and tagged in traces.
- Scheduler: must be able to schedule speculative tasks with different priority and preemption semantics relative to main model inferences.
- KV cache: prefix and KV caches should be consistent between speculative and final paths. Speculative outputs must not pollute persistent caches unless validated.
- Model integration layer: model adapters must expose a speculative profile describing resource footprint, expected quality delta, and compatible kernels/quantization.

2) Flow (happy path)
- Request arrives for generation. Runtime evaluates speculative eligibility via policy (model supports speculative, request size under thresholds, cold start state).
- If eligible, schedule speculative worker using speculative profile. This worker uses a smaller model or optimized kernel and returns candidate tokens or n best sequences.
- Meanwhile the full model is scheduled normally. When full model returns, compare tokens to speculative candidate. If match or within acceptable divergence per policy, accept speculative tokens and short-circuit. Otherwise, replace with full model outputs.
- On match, update ephemeral metrics and optionally increment a validated success counter used to tune policies.

3) Cache handling rules
- Ephemeral-only by default: speculative outputs are kept in ephemeral (request-scoped) caches. Do not write to global prefix or KV cache unless explicit validation occurs.
- Validation window: a speculative result is eligible for cache promotion only after the final model confirms token sequence and Quality checks pass. Promotion is a rare, audited operation.
- Cache keying: ensure speculative runs use identical cache keys as final model (model version, quantization, sequence prefix) to allow comparison. If keys differ, skip promotion and mark as not compatible.

Scheduler and kernel interactions

- Priority model: speculative tasks are lower priority than final model on heavy contention but should be allowed to preempt long tail tasks that are known to be less latency sensitive.
- Admission control: scheduler will impose a speculative concurrency cap per worker pool and per-customer to avoid cost blowouts. Caps are configurable and observed via metrics.
- Kernel hints: model integration profiles should provide kernel hints for speculative execution (e.g., fused attention, int8 path). The runtime will prefer these kernels when scheduling speculative tries.

Model integration checklist (for model owners)

- Speculative profile fields to provide: compatible kernels, memory footprint estimate, expected top1 accuracy vs full model on representative prompt sets, recommended concurrency limit, and a flag whether speculative results are allowed to be cache promoted.
- Tests required: unit-level decoding parity checks, end-to-end latency benchmarks, and a small eval harness comparing quality on a set of canary prompts.
- Metadata: add a speculative capability boolean and an integration doc URL in the model catalog.

Acceptance criteria and metrics

Core metrics to track for canary and rollout phases. Each metric is defined as per request and aggregated at 1m/5m/1h windows and per model/customer.

- Success rate of speculative short-circuits: fraction of eligible requests where speculative result matched or was within allowed divergence. Target for initial Canary: >= 85% for conversational workloads, >= 75% for open generation.
- Quality delta: measure distribution of normalized edit distance and logprob delta between speculative token and final token. Thresholds: median edit distance <= 0.15 tokens per 100, 95p <= 2 tokens.
- User visible regressions: number of requests leading to critical failure modes (toxic output, hallucination) attributed to speculative path. Target: zero for Canary.
- Latency improvement: P95 reduction in end-to-end latency for eligible requests. Target: at least 20% P95 improvement for canary traffic.
- Cost delta: additional compute cost from speculative runs vs savings from shorter serving time. Track net cost per 1k requests and ROI.
- Cache consistency events: count of promotions, promotions reverted, and mismatched key incidents.

Canary and rollout plan

Phase 0: Local and unit testing
- Model owners validate speculative profile and run the integration tests.

Phase 1: Internal Canary (eng only)
- Route 0.5% internal traffic, detailed telemetry turned on, keep speculative concurrency low. Run for 7 days and evaluate metrics.

Phase 2: Beta customers
- Expand to selected beta customers with opt-in. Increase concurrency caps. Monitor per-customer metrics and SLAs.

Phase 3: Gradual rollout
- Ramp up to 25% of production eligible traffic over 2 weeks if KPIs meet thresholds. Default policies conservative; per-customer overrides allowed.

Phase 4: GA
- Open to all customers after 6 weeks of stable metrics and postmortem of any incidents.

Rollback procedures

- Automated fast rollback: if any of the key safety signals cross thresholds (user visible regressions > 0 or quality delta spike beyond defined abort thresholds), flag triggers and immediately disable speculative execution globally while preserving logs for postmortem.
- Gradual rollback: for cross-customer quality degradations without immediate safety triggers, reduce concurrency caps and disable promotions while investigating.
- Per-customer rollback: ability to disable speculative for specific customers via feature flag and policy service.

Operational requirements and observability

- Traces and logs: annotate traces with speculative boolean, profile id, kernel hint, and cache promotion decisions.
- Dashboards: speculative success rate, quality delta histogram, latency improvement P50/P95, speculative concurrency, and cost ROI.
- Alerts: alert on drops in success rate, spikes in edit distance, any promotion reverts, and user visible regression counts.

Open questions and risks

- Risk of silent quality degradation for corner-case prompts. Mitigation: maintain a curated prompt corpus that runs through both paths periodically.
- Potential for increased overall cost if speculative concurrency and failure mode are not tuned. Mitigation: strict per-customer caps and chargeback visibility.
- Cache complexity and correctness when models change versions or quantization. Mitigation: strong keying rules and promotion audits.

Next steps and action items

- Finalize speculative profile schema and add to model catalog API. Owner: Riley Kapoor. Due: 2026-03-01.
- Implement ephemeral-only cache mode and promotion API. Owner: Samir Patel. Due: 2026-03-15.
- Build telemetry dashboard and set alert thresholds. Owner: Elena Martinez. Due: 2026-03-10.
- Run internal canary on the staging cluster. Owner: eng-serving-runtime. Target start: 2026-03-20.

Appendix: quick glossary

- Speculative short-circuit: when the speculative output is accepted and final model result is not returned to the client.
- Promotion: moving speculative-validated outputs into global KV/prefix cache.
- Profile: metadata supplied by model owner describing speculative execution characteristics.
